API reference¶

Everything in the first table is exported from the top-level windvg package; the document layer’s spec classes live in windvg.document.

Core (windvg)¶

.. py:module:: windvg

windvg: parametric perimeter drawing.

Draw polygons and circles, place anchors on their boundaries by traveling a percentage of the perimeter from a start point in a chosen winding direction, and export scenes to TinyVG or SVG.

   import windvg as wv

   circle = wv.Circle((100, 100), 60)
   scene = wv.Scene(200, 200)
   scene.fill(wv.star_polygon(circle, 5, 2), wv.rgb(0.95, 0.8, 0.2))
   scene.write_tinyvg("star.tvg")
   scene.write_svg("star.svg")

.. py:class:: Anchor(shape: ~windvg.shapes.Shape, start_distance: float, direction: ~windvg.shapes.Orientation) :module: windvg :canonical: windvg.anchor.Anchor

Bases: :py:class:object

A starting location on a shape plus a travel direction.

point(pct) returns the boundary point reached by traveling pct percent of the shape’s full perimeter from the anchor’s start, in the anchor’s direction. Values wrap around via modulo, so point(150) is the same location as point(50), and negative percentages travel the other way.

.. py:method:: Anchor.tangent(pct: float = 0.0) -> ~windvg.geometry.Point :module: windvg

  Unit vector of travel at `pct`, following the anchor's direction.

.. py:method:: Anchor.offset(pct: float = 0.0, d: float = 0.0) -> ~windvg.geometry.Point :module: windvg

  Point at `pct` displaced perpendicular to travel by `d`.

  Positive `d` moves to the left of the travel direction, which is
  outward for clockwise tracks and inward for counter-clockwise ones.

.. py:method:: Anchor.at(pct: float) -> ~windvg.anchor.Anchor :module: windvg

  A new anchor whose start is this anchor's position after traveling `pct`.

.. py:class:: Arc(center: tuple[float, float] | ~windvg.geometry.Point, radius: float, start_deg: float, sweep_deg: float) :module: windvg :canonical: windvg.shapes.Arc

Bases: :py:class:~windvg.shapes.Shape

A partial circle, stroke-only (combine with to_pie/to_chord later for fillable wedges once Path exists).

The track starts at start_deg and travels sweep_deg degrees; positive sweeps run visually clockwise on screen. As an open track, travel beyond its ends clamps to the endpoints.

.. py:method:: Arc.perimeter() -> float :module: windvg

  Total length of the boundary.

.. py:method:: Arc.point_at_distance(d: float) -> ~windvg.geometry.Point :module: windvg

  Point at arc-length distance `d` from the shape origin.

  `d` is measured along the positive (visually clockwise) direction.
  Closed tracks wrap via modulo; open tracks (Polyline, Arc) clamp to
  [0, perimeter].

.. py:method:: Arc.tangent_at_distance(d: float) -> ~windvg.geometry.Point :module: windvg

  Unit tangent at arc-length `d`, along the positive travel direction.

.. py:method:: Arc.project(pt: ~windvg.geometry.Point) -> float :module: windvg

  Arc-length position (0..perimeter) of the boundary point nearest to `pt`.

.. py:method:: Arc.bbox() -> tuple[~windvg.geometry.Point, ~windvg.geometry.Point] :module: windvg

  Axis-aligned bounding box as (min corner, max corner), y-down.

  The base implementation samples the track; shapes override with exact
  analytic bounds where possible.

.. py:property:: Arc.winding_sign :module: windvg :type: int

  +1 if the shape's natural parameterization runs visually clockwise.

.. py:property:: Arc.closed :module: windvg :type: bool

  closed tracks wrap distances, open ones clamp.

  :type: Whether the track loops

.. py:class:: GridCellPoint(node: str, col: int, row: int, offset: ~windvg.geometry.Point | None = None) :module: windvg :canonical: windvg.document.GridCellPoint

Bases: :py:class:object

A point expressed in another node’s grid-guide cell coordinates.

Resolves to the referenced grid’s origin + (col * dx, row * dy), plus offset when given, so a shape can snap to cell (1, 0) while staying parametric — the generated code never hardcodes the pixel position.

.. py:class:: GridGuideSpec(origin: object = (0.0, 0.0), cols: int = 8, rows: int = 6, dx: float = 40.0, dy: float = 40.0) :module: windvg :canonical: windvg.document.GridGuideSpec

Bases: :py:class:object

A non-drawing lattice used for snapping and grid-cell references.

Expands to no shapes, so a grid-guide node renders and exports nothing; grid_cell point references resolve against its origin and spacing.

.. py:class:: Polyline(points: list[~windvg.geometry.Point] | tuple[~windvg.geometry.Point, …]) :module: windvg :canonical: windvg.shapes.Polyline

Bases: :py:class:~windvg.shapes.Shape

An open chain of points.

Strokable but not fillable. Its positive direction is the order the points were given, so CW means forward along the chain and CCW means backward. Unlike closed tracks, travel does not wrap: distances outside [0, perimeter] clamp to the nearer endpoint.

.. py:function:: star(center: tuple[float, float] | ~windvg.geometry.Point, outer_radius: float, inner_radius: float, points: int = 5, start_angle_deg: float = 0.0) -> ~windvg.shapes.Polygon :module: windvg

A classic star shape with alternating outer and inner vertices.

.. py:function:: star_polygon(circle: ~windvg.shapes.Circle, points: int, skip: int) -> ~windvg.shapes.Polygon :module: windvg

A star drawn with the anchor system itself.

Places points anchors evenly around circle and connects each one to the anchor skip positions along, producing shapes like the pentagram (star_polygon(circle, 5, 2)). Requires gcd(points, skip) == 1 so the traversal visits every anchor exactly once.

Document specs (windvg.document)¶

.. py:module:: windvg.document

Serializable, parametric scene documents.

A Document is the persistent form of a drawing: an ordered list of named, visible-or-hidden nodes, each an operation (fill/stroke/outline_fill) over a parametric shape spec with a paint. Documents convert to and from plain JSON dicts, resolve to a renderable Scene, and translate to and from readable Python source — the round trip editors need:

   code ──Document.from_code──▶ document ──resolve──▶ Scene ──▶ TinyVG/SVG
     ▲                            │
     └──────generate_code─────────┘

Points inside specs may be literal [x, y] pairs or parametric references: {“anchor”: {“node”: “gear”, “pct”: 25, “direction”: “cw”}} — resolved against another node’s shape — or {“grid_cell”: {“node”: “grid1”, “col”: 1, “row”: 0}} — resolved against a grid guide’s lattice. References keep visual edits parametric: the generated code never hardcodes resolved pixel positions.

Paths (windvg.path)¶

.. py:module:: windvg.path

Paths: mixed line/curve segments as tracks, with holes via subpaths.

Instructions mirror the TinyVG/SVG toolset (line, quadratic/cubic Bezier, circle and ellipse arcs, close) in SVG-style endpoint parameterization, so a Path exports 1:1 to both formats. Flattening (used for arc-length queries) is adaptive with a configurable tolerance; exact instructions are still what gets written to files.

A Path may hold several subpaths; filled paths use the even-odd rule, so an inner subpath carves a hole.

.. py:class:: Line(to: ‘Point’) :module: windvg.path

.. py:class:: Quad(ctrl: ‘Point’, to: ‘Point’) :module: windvg.path

.. py:class:: Cubic(c1: ‘Point’, c2: ‘Point’, to: ‘Point’) :module: windvg.path

.. py:class:: ArcCircle(radius: ‘float’, large: ‘bool’, sweep_cw: ‘bool’, to: ‘Point’) :module: windvg.path

.. py:class:: ArcEllipse(rx: ‘float’, ry: ‘float’, rotation_deg: ‘float’, large: ‘bool’, sweep_cw: ‘bool’, to: ‘Point’) :module: windvg.path

.. py:class:: Close() :module: windvg.path

.. py:class:: SubPath(start: ‘Point’, instructions: ‘tuple[Instruction, …]’) :module: windvg.path

.. py:class:: Path(subpaths: ~collections.abc.Sequence[~windvg.path.SubPath], tolerance: float = 0.1) :module: windvg.path

One or more subpaths of mixed line/curve instructions.

Track queries run on a flattened approximation with the given tolerance; export stays exact. Filled paths apply the even-odd rule across subpaths.

.. py:method:: Path.perimeter() -> float :module: windvg.path

  Total length of the boundary.

.. py:method:: Path.point_at_distance(d: float) -> ~windvg.geometry.Point :module: windvg.path

  Point at arc-length distance `d` from the shape origin.

  `d` is measured along the positive (visually clockwise) direction.
  Closed tracks wrap via modulo; open tracks (Polyline, Arc) clamp to
  [0, perimeter].

.. py:method:: Path.tangent_at_distance(d: float) -> ~windvg.geometry.Point :module: windvg.path

  Unit tangent at arc-length `d`, along the positive travel direction.

.. py:method:: Path.project(pt: ~windvg.geometry.Point) -> float :module: windvg.path

  Arc-length position (0..perimeter) of the boundary point nearest to `pt`.

.. py:property:: Path.closed :module: windvg.path :type: bool

  closed tracks wrap distances, open ones clamp.

  :type: Whether the track loops

.. py:property:: Path.winding_sign :module: windvg.path :type: int

  +1 if the shape's natural parameterization runs visually clockwise.

.. py:method:: Path.bbox() -> tuple[~windvg.geometry.Point, ~windvg.geometry.Point] :module: windvg.path

  Axis-aligned bounding box as (min corner, max corner), y-down.

  The base implementation samples the track; shapes override with exact
  analytic bounds where possible.

.. py:method:: Path.segment_count() -> int :module: windvg.path

  How many TinyVG path segments the path encodes as.

.. py:class:: PathBuilder(start: tuple[float, float] | ~windvg.geometry.Point) :module: windvg.path

Fluent constructor for Paths, one subpath at a time.

path = ( PathBuilder((10, 10)) .line_to((90, 10)) .arc_circle_to(20, (90, 50), sweep_cw=True) .close() .build() )

.. py:method:: PathBuilder.move_to(pt: tuple[float, float] | ~windvg.geometry.Point) -> ~windvg.path.PathBuilder :module: windvg.path

  Finish the current subpath and start a new one at `pt`.
